clue.text: Club followed by diamonds shortly turning out unexpectedly

indicators.note: the club comes first and the shortened diamonds come after it

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player leads a club, then a diamond, and the hand plays out in a way nobody expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture makes club and diamonds look like suits; here one is a golf club and the other is gangster slang for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ironic happens contrary to what was expected, often with a wry twist of fate.

clue.text: Loosen up? Right! Drink up? Wrong!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
X is the cross a marker puts beside a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to unwind and agrees, then told to down a drink and objects.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamations look like a dialogue; the second 'up' turns the drink round, and X stands for wrong as a teacher's cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to become less tense, to unwind or ease off.

clue.text: Number go into State by night

indicators.note: the go is placed into the state's letters

parts.note: Cal is a short form for California
a turn is a go, as in 'whose go is it?'

explanation.surface: An instruction to dial a number and enter a state after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Number reads as a figure, but it gives the abbreviation NO; Cal for California is the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes what happens or is active during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Nut takes the money you and I put up

parts.note: cash is money in hand

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the pronoun is written upwards

parts.note: we is the pronoun for you and I together

explanation.surface: A lunatic pockets the cash that the two of us stumped up.
explanation.walkthrough: Nut looks like a madman who takes our money; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a kidney-shaped edible nut from a tropical tree.

clue.text: Bear, strange to relate

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the following word are set in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: The stock phrase 'strange to relate' introduces an odd story, here about a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: TO stands unchanged at the front; only RELATE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it or endure it, the same sense as the verb here.

clue.text: Gay work — beat geographers dance to

indicators.note: the letters of beat geographers dance around to form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cheerful piece of music to which tired map-makers dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Gay is John Gay, the 18th-century English dramatist, not the adjective; his best-known work is this ballad opera.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay wrote this 1728 ballad opera, so it is a work by Gay.

clue.text: This prevents chaps — evil pals — misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave are out of order, so evil pals are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something keeping blokes away from their wicked, unruly friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaps reads as men; it is chapped skin, the cracking that cold weather causes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lip salve is a balm rubbed on the lips to stop them chapping.

clue.text: Bolshy bishop participating in dance

indicators.note: the bishop takes part inside the dance's letters

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A truculent cleric joins in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for defiant or uncooperative, the attitude of a rebel.

clue.text: Delivered carpeting — checked the completion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gave a telling-off, a carpeting being a British word for a reprimand
second meaning: marked an item done with a tick on a list

explanation.walkthrough: Carpeting looks like floor covering being delivered; in Britain to be 'carpeted' is to be summoned and scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both scolded someone and marked something as done with a check mark.

clue.text: Disreputable relation, a purveyor of wool

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the family member who has brought disgrace
second meaning: a literal dark-fleeced sheep, which supplies wool

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playfully literal, echoing the nursery rhyme 'Baa, baa, black sheep, have you any wool?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the family member regarded as a disgrace; the literal animal supplies fleece.

clue.text: Support for part of the body

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the rear of the torso

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single phrase about a brace or truss; split it after 'Support' to get two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for championing someone and the name of the rear torso.

clue.text: Apology for interrupting dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the polite phrase said when cutting in
second meaning: a ballroom dance in which partners may be claimed by cutting in

explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is a social dance where anyone can tap a dancer's shoulder and take over the partner, so the two senses are linked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite apology and also the name of a ballroom dance where cutting in is allowed.

clue.text: Napping when PM returned

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: the Prime Minister's name is read backwards

parts.note: Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century

explanation.surface: Someone was dozing when the Prime Minister came back.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the afternoon time; it is a Prime Minister, Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Napping is sleeping lightly, and asleep describes someone in that state.

clue.text: Wife's admirer coming round to dance attendance

indicators.note: the admirer's letters come round, enclosing the wife

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife's suitor drops by so he can wait on her hand and foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter and act servilely, as one who dances attendance does.

clue.text: Flattery — grown-up welcomes a tiny bit

indicators.note: the grown-up takes the letter in, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up
taken as written
an ion is an electrically charged particle, a very small bit of matter

explanation.surface: An adult accepts just a smidgen of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive admiration or praise, a strong form of flattery.

clue.text: My father is a regulator

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old British slang for one's father, as in 'the guv'nor'
second meaning: a device controlling engine speed

explanation.walkthrough: The sentence suggests a strict parent; in fact it pairs a slang term for dad with a mechanical regulating device.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is a speed-limiting mechanism on an engine and also slang for one's dad or boss.

clue.text: Mother supporting scoundrel in European city

indicators.note: in a down entry the mother sits underneath, holding up the scoundrel

parts.note: rotter is dated British slang for a scoundrel
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A mother backs her no-good son somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major port city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Evil hypnotist's revolting leavings

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the hypnotist himself

indicators.note: revolting means in revolt, so the letters of leavings rise up into a new order

explanation.surface: The disgusting scraps left behind by a wicked mesmerist.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like 'disgusting', describing the leftovers; read it as rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the sinister mesmerist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, now a byword for a manipulator.

clue.text: Visit a lay-by in Jersey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... is to steer a car off the road into a stopping place

explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island; it is the knitted garment. A lay-by is a British roadside parking strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a sweater pulled on over the head, also called a jersey.

clue.text: Following coughing attack, turned and spat

indicators.note: the attack is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a fit is a bout, as in a coughing fit
F is the abbreviation for following, as in 'pp. 12f'

explanation.surface: After a fit of coughing, someone turned away and spat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spat reads as the verb of spitting, natural after coughing; it is the noun for a petty quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor quarrel, the same as a spat.

clue.text: Dog worried clergyman

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A dog harassed the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: Worried reads as an adjective; take it as the past tense of eat in its sense of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant priest in a parish, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Fool has hidden silver in some water

indicators.note: the fool contains the silver, concealing it

parts.note: a loon is a crazy or foolish person
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An idiot has stashed his silver under the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of salt water cut off from the sea by a reef or sandbank.

clue.text: Cat — what dead one may do (not black)?

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the black out

parts.note: the dead cat bounce is a stock-market saying: even a dead cat bounces if dropped from high enough
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A grim riddle about what a dead cat might get up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'Cat' the subject of the riddle, so 'dead one' means a dead cat, whose bounce is the market jargon for a brief recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Cry stifled, as soon as wealth is manifest

definitions.note: a clause describing what the noun is: wealth on show

indicators.note: the cry is smothered inside the other word

parts.note: once means as soon as, as in 'once you arrive'
to pule is to whimper or cry weakly

explanation.surface: Whimpering is hushed the moment riches appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is lavish, ostentatious richness, wealth on open display.

clue.text: Examination initiated in vehicle — this reveals something missing

indicators.note: that letter sits inside the vehicle's letters

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle

indicators.note: initiated means begun, so only the starting letter of examination is used

parts.note: initiated takes just the opening letter of examination

explanation.surface: An inspection begun in a car turns up something that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A caret is the proofreader's mark showing where a missing word or letter should be inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: The proofreading symbol marks the spot where an omitted word or character must be added.

clue.text: Right to give story a point

parts.note: a story is a lie, as when a child tells stories
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The privilege of adding a final flourish to a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim: the right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: King's salad used to include this

definitions.text: King's salad used to include this

parts.words: King's salad used to include this
parts.note: reads as a royal menu, but the possessive king's name is itself an old salad plant, once eaten and now rarely

explanation.walkthrough: Alexanders is a celery-like plant once grown as a pot-herb and salad vegetable; the clue suggests it belongs to King Alexander.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexanders, Smyrnium olusatrum, was a common vegetable and salad plant before celery replaced it.

clue.text: Very good — a cake decoration

parts.note: angelic means extremely well-behaved
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a pastry chef's topping: excellent, a fine decoration for a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is a plant whose candied green stems are used to decorate cakes.

clue.text: Net I weaved with my needle

indicators.note: weaved suggests threads moved in and out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describing knitting or making a net with a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: Needle looks like the sewing tool in the craft picture; it is the noun for hostility, as in a 'needle match'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle in British usage means ill feeling or antagonism between rivals, the same as hostility.
